statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases from 24 to 21 because the recovery off the session low has extended into a genuine two-sided range, while Stress stays high at 70 as crude keeps extending.

The upper end of that range is new: at 14:28 UTC the session high was 29,128.99, so price has since traded roughly 275 points above the 28,992.25 low, made a higher high, and then faded back toward the middle. Nasdaq-100 futures were 29,232.00, -0.95%, about 192 points above their own 29,040.25 low. That sequence is two-sided trade rather than the repeated extension seen between 09:00 and 13:00 UTC, and it is what lowers Tail from 24 to 21. Volatility is decaying with it: VIX is 15.36 after a 16.06 session high. Stress stays high at 70 because the macro driver has not eased. WTI is $89.71, +4.60% on the day and above the $87.62 seen at the previous assessment, with Brent $94.14; the US 10-year is 4.774% after a 4.790% intraday high described as the highest since January 2025, the 30-year has traded toward multi-decade highs near 5.24%, and the 2-year is 4.387%. Equities recovering while crude extends is a cross-asset conflict, which under the inherited risk definition raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. Today's releases were modest misses: ISM Manufacturing 54.6 versus 55.2 expected with Prices unchanged at 71.1, and JOLTS July openings little changed at 7.3 million. The live US-Iran conflict remains the unresolved mechanism: two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night and further US strikes are reported to be under consideration, so a delayed second leg cannot be ruled out. Mapped policy state: WATCH, with a narrow danger window over the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour. Delayed Finviz cross-asset context from 15:34 UTC is consistent with this picture: NQ -1.02%, VX +2.05%, CL +2.81%, all seven tracked semiconductors lower and six of eight megacaps lower on the latest session.
headline: Nasdaq-100 builds a two-sided 28,992-29,267 range after the morning down-leg, but crude extends to $89.71 WTI and long yields hold near multi-decade highs
body:
The decisive change this hour is structural. Through the 09:00-13:00 UTC sequence the Nasdaq-100 repeatedly extended with price sitting within a few points of each new low, which is exactly the pattern the Tail measure targets. That pattern is now broken. After the 14:00 UTC data block the index retraced, and it has since printed a session high of 29,267.42, about 275 points above the 28,992.25 low and well above the 29,128.99 high that stood at the previous assessment. It then faded back to 29,143.98 at 16:25 UTC. A higher high followed by a controlled fade into the middle of the range is orderly price discovery, not a failed-retracement path. Nasdaq-100 futures confirm it at 29,232.00, roughly 192 points off their own 29,040.25 low.

Volatility is following the same path. VIX is 15.36 against a 16.06 session high and a 14.43 previous close, so the premium built during the morning is being released rather than extended.

What has not eased is the macro backdrop, and this is why Stress stays at 70 rather than falling with Tail. Crude has extended since the previous assessment rather than stabilised: WTI is $89.71, +4.60% on the day and above the $87.62 printed at 14:33 UTC, with Brent at $94.14. The US 10-year is 4.774% after touching 4.790%, its highest intraday level since January 2025, the 30-year has traded toward multi-decade highs around 5.24%, and the 2-year is 4.387%, up about 3 basis points. Equities repairing while the inflation and rates channel keeps deteriorating is a genuine cross-asset conflict. Under the inherited risk definition that reduces directional conviction and supports a high Stress reading; it does not by itself constitute the persistent one-way structure that Tail measures.

The scheduled data are already resolved and were modest misses rather than shocks. ISM Manufacturing printed 54.6 for August against 55.2 expected and 55.6 prior, an eighth consecutive month of expansion, with New Orders 53.7, Employment 51.2 and Prices unchanged at 71.1. JOLTS job openings for July were little changed at 7.3 million against 7.300 million expected. Neither print is the driver of today's move.

The unresolved element is geopolitical rather than macroeconomic. Two oil tankers, one Saudi and one South Korean owned, were struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night, ending roughly a month of relative calm in the US-Iran conflict. Live reporting has the US administration considering further strikes while Qatar presses mediation and Iran signals openness to talks. That is an active, unscheduled mechanism capable of producing a second leg at any hour, which is why Tail eases to 21 rather than into the EA_ON band despite the observed retracement.

Delayed Finviz cross-asset context collected at 15:34 UTC is used only as supporting confirmation and not as live price-path evidence. It shows NQ -1.02%, ES -0.49%, VX +2.05%, CL +2.81% and GC -1.56%, with all seven tracked semiconductors negative on the latest session, six of eight megacaps lower, and Software - Infrastructure -2.15% and Semiconductor Equipment & Materials -2.74% at the industry level. That alignment is consistent with a risk-reducing session but is not evidence of the current intraday path.

Mapped policy state: WATCH, with Tail below the blocking threshold. The danger window is kept narrow and covers the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour into the cash close, which is the remaining scheduled structural risk point of the session.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 15:00 UTC hour on 1 September has none and is marked unavailable. The first sixteen slots, covering the 31 August US session and the overnight hours, sat in the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 13 and mode mixed, while Stress drifted from 52 up to 58 as crude firmed and long yields climbed. The regime changed at 08:00 UTC on 1 September, when Tail moved to 22 with mode trend-down. It reached 26 at 09:00 UTC for the first BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES reading of the sequence, held at 25 through 10:00 and 11:00 UTC, rose to 28 at 12:00 UTC as the base broke, and peaked at 31 with Stress 75 at 13:00 UTC after a third consecutive hourly extension into the cash open. The 14:00 UTC assessment stepped back to 24 with mode event/whipsaw once the first genuine retracement appeared. Stress rose from 65 to 75 and then eased to 71 across the sequence, and confidence stayed between 84 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is that the 1 September rates, crude and geopolitical repricing continues to resolve into two-sided trade. The projection starts from an observed higher high rather than from an extension, so Tail begins at 21 for the current 16:00 UTC hour and eases to 20 across the New York lunch hours on the condition that the 28,992.25 low holds. A single lift to 23 with Stress 70 at 19:00 UTC carries the power-hour checkpoint into the 20:00 UTC cash close, treated as a scheduled structural allowance rather than an observed path. From 21:00 UTC Tail falls into the EA_ON band and bottoms at 12 through the Asian hours as ranges compress, then rises gradually to 17 across the European morning. The final slots carry conditional checkpoints on 2 September: 19 at 12:00 UTC for the ADP employment print at 12:15 UTC, 20 at 13:00 UTC for the US cash open, 20 at 14:00 UTC for Factory Orders and the EIA crude inventory report, and 19 at 15:00 UTC as mid-session trade normalises. No forecast hour reaches the blocking threshold, because a scheduled event is a checkpoint rather than observed one-way structure. Confidence decays from 89 to 58 with the age of the live price-path observation.
